feedback.queue.stillWaiting_one.description: Status line of the "Suggest an improvement" dialog after "Try again" failed. {{count}} is how many saved messages are still unsent; this form is for exactly one.

feedback.queue.stillWaiting_other.text: Still couldn't send them. All {{count}} are kept on this device and will try again by themselves.
feedback.queue.stillWaiting_other.description: Status line of the "Suggest an improvement" dialog after "Try again" failed. {{count}} is how many saved messages are still unsent.

feedback.queue.flushed_one.text: Your saved feedback has been sent.
feedback.queue.flushed_one.description: Brief message at the bottom of the screen when a message saved while offline was sent. {{count}} is how many were sent; this form is for exactly one.

feedback.queue.flushed_other.text: Your {{count}} saved feedback messages have been sent.
feedback.queue.flushed_other.description: Brief message at the bottom of the screen when messages saved while offline were sent. {{count}} is how many.

feedback.draftSaved.text: Your request draft was saved. Reopen Suggest an improvement to finish it.
feedback.draftSaved.description: Brief message at the bottom of the screen after the page reloaded while a request was being written. "Suggest an improvement" is the dialog's name; translate it as its heading is translated.

feedback.submit.post.description: Text of the main button of the "Suggest an improvement" dialog: posts the request. "Post" is a verb; a request is an item asking for a change.

feedback.submit.saveForLater.description: Text of the main button of the "Suggest an improvement" dialog while there is no connection: keeps the request on this device and sends it when the connection returns.

feedback.submit.posting.description: Text of the main button of the "Suggest an improvement" dialog while the request is being sent.

feedback.submit.saved.description: Text of the main button of the "Suggest an improvement" dialog, disabled, after the request was saved on this device for sending later.

feedback.submit.posted.description: Text of the main button of the "Suggest an improvement" dialog, disabled, after the request was posted.

feedback.error.file.text: Couldn't file this right now. Please try again later.
feedback.error.file.description: Red status line of the "suggest an improvement" dialog when the server failed to post the request. To file is to post it.

feedback.error.network.description: Red status line of the "suggest an improvement" dialog when the server's answer could not be read or the request could not be saved for later.

feedback.fix.failedRequest.text: Could not open a fix just now. You can try again from the request on the board.
feedback.fix.failedRequest.description: Brief message at the bottom of the screen when "Build it now with a coding agent" could not start a change. A fix is a change that solves the request; the board is the app's list of requests.

feedback.fix.failedIssue.text: Could not open a fix just now. You can try again from the issue on the board.
feedback.fix.failedIssue.description: Brief message at the bottom of the screen when "Try a fix yourself" could not start a change. A fix is a change that solves the issue; the board is the app's list of issues.

feedback.notice.pair.description: How two complete sentences are joined when the confirmation of a posted request says several things on one line, for example "Posted to Run Club. Pledged 1 kudos as a bounty. 4 left this week." {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next sentence. Only what goes between them is translated.

feedback.posted.app.description: Green status line of the "suggest an improvement" dialog after a request was posted to an app. {{app}} is the app's name. A full sentence, with its full stop.

feedback.posted.thisApp.description: Green status line of the "suggest an improvement" dialog after a request was posted to the open app, when its name is not known. A full sentence, with its full stop.

feedback.posted.platform.description: Green status line of the "suggest an improvement" dialog after a request was posted to Homeroom itself. Homeroom is the product's name.

feedback.first.title.description: Heading shown in place of the form after a person posted their very first request.

feedback.first.intro.text: You’ve helped make this app better. Want to take the next step?
feedback.first.intro.description: Line under the first-request heading, above buttons offering what to do next.

feedback.first.posted.description: Green line of the first-request moment: confirms the request was posted.

feedback.first.savedPosted.text: Your saved request has been posted.
feedback.first.savedPosted.description: Green line of the first-request moment when the request had been saved while offline and was posted when the dialog was opened again.

feedback.first.savedSent.text: Your saved feedback has been sent.
feedback.first.savedSent.description: Green line of the first-request moment when the request had been saved while offline and was sent in the background.

feedback.first.fix.description: Button of the first-request moment: starts a change that solves the request, written with the coding agent.

feedback.first.fixNote.default.text: Start with a draft you can edit before sending it to the coding agent.
feedback.first.fixNote.default.description: Note under the "Try a fix yourself" button of the first-request moment. The coding agent is the AI that writes the code.

feedback.first.fixNote.needAccess.text: You need collaborator access to try a fix. You can still explore the board.
feedback.first.fixNote.needAccess.description: Note under the disabled "Try a fix yourself" button when the person may not build changes for this app. The board is the app's list of requests.

feedback.first.fixNote.noBoard.text: This repository does not have an app board you can access here.
feedback.first.fixNote.noBoard.description: Note under the disabled "Try a fix yourself" button when the request went somewhere that has no board to open.

feedback.first.board.description: Button of the first-request moment: opens the app's board, its list of requests and proposals.

feedback.first.mine.description: Button of the first-request moment: opens the list of this person's own requests on their profile.

feedback.sent.title.description: Heading of the confirmation shown in place of the form after a request was posted, before the place it went to is known.

feedback.sent.postedApp.description: Heading of the confirmation after a request was posted to an app and the assistant is building it. {{app}} is the app's name. No full stop.

feedback.sent.postedThisApp.description: Heading of the confirmation after a request was posted to the open app, when its name is not known. No full stop.

feedback.sent.postedPlatform.description: Heading of the confirmation after a request was posted to Homeroom itself. Homeroom is the product's name. No full stop.

feedback.sent.thanksApp.description: Heading of the confirmation after a request was posted to an app. {{app}} is the app's name.

feedback.sent.thanksThisApp.description: Heading of the confirmation after a request was posted to the open app, when its name is not known.

feedback.sent.thanksPlatform.description: Heading of the confirmation after a request was posted to Homeroom itself. Homeroom is the product's name.

feedback.sent.thanksGroup.description: Heading of the confirmation after a request went to the people who run an app rather than to the assistant. {{app}} is the app's name; the group is that app's members.

feedback.sent.thanksThisGroup.text: Thanks! Sent to this app's group
feedback.sent.thanksThisGroup.description: Heading of the confirmation after a request went to the people who run the open app, when its name is not known. The group is the app's members.

feedback.sent.botTitle.description: Heading of the confirmation after a request was posted and the assistant (Homeroom bot) has started building it.

feedback.sent.line.text: Your idea is on the board now. Find it on your profile, under Your requests.
feedback.sent.line.description: Line of the confirmation after a request was posted. The board is the app's list of requests; "Your requests" is the name of a list on the profile screen.

feedback.sent.botLine_one.text: Homeroom bot is building it now, usually about {{count}} minutes. You'll get a message when it's ready to try.
feedback.sent.botLine_one.description: Line of the confirmation when the assistant is building the request. {{count}} is the usual number of minutes a build takes. "Homeroom bot" is the assistant's name and stays as it is.

feedback.sent.botLine_other.text: Homeroom bot is building it now, usually about {{count}} minutes. You'll get a message when it's ready to try.
feedback.sent.botLine_other.description: Line of the confirmation when the assistant is building the request. {{count}} is the usual number of minutes a build takes. "Homeroom bot" is the assistant's name and stays as it is.

feedback.sent.firstTitle.description: Bold line in a green box of the confirmation when this was the person's very first request and the assistant is building it.

feedback.sent.firstLine.named.description: Line under "Your first request!" in the confirmation. {{app}} is the name of the app the request was for.

feedback.sent.firstLine.unnamed.text: You just helped shape this app.
feedback.sent.firstLine.unnamed.description: Line under "Your first request!" in the confirmation, when the app's name is not known.

feedback.sent.chat.description: Main button of the confirmation when the assistant is building the request: opens the chat with Homeroom bot. "Open" is a verb.

feedback.sent.mine.description: Button of the confirmation after a request was posted: opens the list of this person's own requests on their profile.

feedback.sent.fix.text: Build it now with a coding agent
feedback.sent.fix.description: Small link at the foot of the confirmation when the assistant is building the request: lets the person write the change themselves with the AI coding agent instead. "Build" is a verb.

members.title.full.description: Heading of the dialog that lists an app's collaborators, approvers and admins and sets how its proposals are approved.

members.title.approvals.description: Heading of the same dialog for Homeroom's own app, where it holds only the approval settings.

members.error.appLoading.text: This app is still loading. Open Members & approvals again in a moment.
members.error.appLoading.description: Error at the top of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when it was opened before the app's details had loaded. "Members & approvals" is the dialog's name.

members.invite.label.description: Label of the username field at the top of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: the person typed there is invited to collaborate on the app.

members.invite.placeholder.description: Greyed text inside the empty invite field of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app. Lower case, like a username.

members.invite.sending.description: Shown under the invite field of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app while the invitation is being sent.

members.invite.sent.description: Shown under the invite field of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app after the invitation was sent. {{username}} is the invited person's username; keep the check mark and the @.

members.collaborators.heading.description: Label above the list of people who may build changes for the app, in the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.collaborators.empty.description: Shown in the "Collaborators" list of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when nobody has been invited.

members.collaborators.loadFailed.description: Error in the "Collaborators" list of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app. {{reason}} is a short technical reason such as "HTTP 500".

members.collaborators.tag.creator.description: Small tag after a username in the "Collaborators" list of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: this person created the app. Lower case.

members.collaborators.tag.invited.description: Small tag after a username in the "Collaborators" list of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: this person was invited and has not accepted yet. Lower case.

members.collaborators.revoke.description: Button on a row of the "Collaborators" list of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app for someone who has not accepted yet: withdraws their invitation.

members.collaborators.revokeTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Revoke" button on a row of the "Collaborators" list of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.collaborators.leave.description: Button on the viewer's own row of the "Collaborators" list of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: stops being a collaborator of the app. A verb.

members.collaborators.leaveTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Leave" button on the viewer's own row of the "Collaborators" list of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app. "Leave" is a verb.

members.collaborators.remove.description: Button on another person's row of the "Collaborators" list of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: removes them as a collaborator.

members.collaborators.removeTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Remove" button on another person's row of the "Collaborators" list of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.collaborators.removeFailed.description: Brief message at the bottom of the screen when removing a collaborator or withdrawing an invitation failed. {{reason}} is the server's explanation or a short technical reason.

members.governance.heading.description: Heading of the section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app that sets who may approve proposals and how many approvals one needs.

members.governance.who.description: Label above the two choices "Everyone" and "Invited approvers" in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.governance.policy.everyone.description: Choice under "Who can approve proposals" in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: any member may approve.

members.governance.policy.invited.description: Choice under "Who can approve proposals" in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: only people invited as approvers may approve.

members.governance.howMany.description: Label above the two choices "Time & majority" and "At least" in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.governance.mode.default.description: Choice under "How many approvals are needed" in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: the usual rule, where a proposal passes after a waiting time with a majority in favour.

members.governance.mode.atLeast.description: Choice under "How many approvals are needed" in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: a fixed minimum number of approvals. A number field follows it, so it reads "At least 3".

members.governance.propose.description: Button beside the number field in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: puts the new number of approvals up as a proposal. A verb.

members.governance.note.text: Changes open a proposal that is voted on under the current rules.
members.governance.note.description: Small note in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: changing the approval settings is itself decided by a vote.

members.governance.noRepository.text: Approval-settings changes are proposed as a dapp.json pull request, and this app has no GitHub repository, so they're unavailable.
members.governance.noRepository.description: Note in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when the settings cannot be changed. dapp.json is a file name and stays as it is.

members.governance.setNumber.text: Set the number of approvals, then tap Propose.
members.governance.setNumber.description: Hint in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app after "At least" was chosen. "Propose" is the button beside the number field; translate it as that button.

members.governance.review.text: Review the initial approvers, then tap Propose.
members.governance.review.description: Hint in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app after "Invited approvers" was chosen and the list of first approvers is shown. "Propose" is the button under that list.

members.governance.confirm.title.description: Title of the confirmation asked before a change to an app's approval settings is put up as a proposal. "Open" is a verb.

members.governance.confirm.message.text: Changing the approval settings opens a proposal that is voted on under the current rules. The change applies after the vote passes and the app redeploys.
members.governance.confirm.message.description: Body of the confirmation asked before a change to an app's approval settings is put up as a proposal.

members.governance.confirm.open.description: Confirming button of that confirmation: creates the proposal. "Open" is a verb.

members.governance.alreadyWaiting.text: A change to who runs this app is already waiting for approval. See it in the Workshop.
members.governance.alreadyWaiting.description: Status in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when an earlier proposal about the app's approvers or admins is undecided. The Workshop is a tab of the app's page; keep it as a name.

members.governance.opened.text: Proposal opened (PR #{{number}}). It needs the group's vote in the Dev tab's vote panel before the new settings apply.
members.governance.opened.description: Status in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app after the change was put up as a proposal. {{number}} is the number of its pull request (PR); keep the # before it. "Dev" is the name of a tab.

members.governance.openedWithWarnings.text: Proposal opened (PR #{{number}}). It needs the group's vote in the Dev tab's vote panel before the new settings apply. Some approver invites could not be sent: {{warnings}}.
members.governance.openedWithWarnings.description: The same status when some of the first approvers could not be invited. {{number}} is the pull request's number; {{warnings}} is the server's list of what went wrong, without a final full stop.

members.governance.failed.text: Could not open the governance proposal: {{reason}}
members.governance.failed.description: Error in the "Proposal approvals" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when the proposal could not be created. {{reason}} is the server's explanation or a short technical reason.

members.initialApprovers.heading.description: Heading of the step in the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app shown after choosing "Invited approvers": who will be the first approvers.

members.initialApprovers.placeholder.description: Greyed text inside the empty username field of the "Initial approvers" step of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.initialApprovers.propose.description: Button of the "Initial approvers" step of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: puts the switch to invited approvers, with the listed people, up as a proposal. A verb.

members.initialApprovers.willBeInvited.description: Small tag after a username in the "Initial approvers" step of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: this person will be invited as an approver once the proposal passes. Lower case.

members.initialApprovers.remove.description: Button on a row of the "Initial approvers" step of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: takes that person off the list of people to invite.

members.initialApprovers.status.current.text: Current approvers stay in place: {{approvers}}. Add more people to invite below (optional).
members.initialApprovers.status.current.description: First line of the "Initial approvers" step of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when the app already has approvers. {{approvers}} is the list of their usernames, each with an @.

members.initialApprovers.status.platform.text: Platform admins can approve proposals until invited approvers are added. Pick some below.
members.initialApprovers.status.platform.description: First line of the "Initial approvers" step of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app for Homeroom's own app, which has no approvers yet.

members.initialApprovers.status.creatorF.text: The app's creator will automatically become the first approver. Add more people to invite below (optional).
members.initialApprovers.status.creatorF.description: First line of the "Initial approvers" step of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when someone other than the app's creator is making the change.

members.initialApprovers.status.youFirst.text: You'll automatically become this app's first approver. Add more people to invite below (optional).
members.initialApprovers.status.youFirst.description: First line of the "Initial approvers" step of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when the app's creator is making the change.

members.approvers.heading.description: Label above the list of people who may approve the app's proposals, in the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.approvers.dormantNote.text: Approvers only take effect when “Who can approve proposals” is set to Invited approvers.
members.approvers.dormantNote.description: Note under the list in the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when approvers exist but the app lets everyone approve. The quoted words are the label and "Invited approvers" the choice in the same dialog; translate them the same way.

members.approvers.invitePlaceholder.description: Greyed text inside the empty username field of the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.approvers.empty.text: No approvers yet. Platform admins can approve proposals until an approver is added.
members.approvers.empty.description: Shown in the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when nobody has been invited as an approver.

members.approvers.loadFailed.description: Error in the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app. {{reason}} is a short technical reason such as "HTTP 500".

members.approvers.tag.invited.description: Small tag after a username in the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: this person was invited as an approver and has not accepted yet. Lower case.

members.approvers.tag.approver.description: Small tag after a username in the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: this person may approve proposals. Lower case.

members.approvers.revoke.description: Button on a row of the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app for someone who has not accepted yet: withdraws their invitation.

members.approvers.revokeTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Revoke" button on a row of the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.approvers.leave.description: Button on the viewer's own row of the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: stops being an approver of this app. A verb.

members.approvers.leaveTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Leave" button on the viewer's own row of the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.approvers.remove.description: Button on another person's row of the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: removes them as an approver.

members.approvers.removeTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Remove" button on another person's row of the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.approvers.removeFailed.description: Brief message at the bottom of the screen when removing an approver or withdrawing their invitation failed. {{reason}} is the server's explanation or a short technical reason.

members.approvers.inviting.description: Shown under the username field of the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app while the invitation is being sent.

members.approvers.invited.description: Shown under the username field of the "Approvers" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app after the invitation was sent. {{username}} is the invited person's username; keep the check mark and the @.

members.appAdmins.heading.description: Label above the list of people who administer the app, in the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.appAdmins.placeholder.description: Greyed text inside the empty username field of the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.appAdmins.propose.description: Button in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: puts the edited list of admins up as a proposal. A verb.

members.appAdmins.empty.text: No app admins yet. App admins can manage this app's settings and force-merge its proposals.
members.appAdmins.empty.description: Shown in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when the app has no admins. To force-merge is to apply a proposal without waiting for the vote.

members.appAdmins.loadFailed.description: Error in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app. {{reason}} is a short technical reason such as "HTTP 500".

members.appAdmins.remove.description: Button on a row of the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: marks that admin for removal in the proposal being prepared.

members.appAdmins.undo.description: Button on a row of the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app marked "will be removed": keeps that admin after all.

members.appAdmins.tag.admin.description: Small tag on a row of the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: this person is an admin of the app now.

members.appAdmins.tag.unregistered.description: Small tag on a row of the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: the username is listed as an admin but nobody has an account with it. Lower case.

members.appAdmins.tag.unregisteredTitle.text: Declared in dapp.json but no account with this username exists yet
members.appAdmins.tag.unregisteredTitle.description: Tooltip of the "not a registered user" tag in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app. dapp.json is a file name and stays as it is.

members.appAdmins.tag.willBeRemoved.description: Small red tag on a row of the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: this admin is removed by the proposal being prepared. Lower case.

members.appAdmins.tag.willBeAdded.description: Small tag on a row of the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: this person is added as an admin by the proposal being prepared. Lower case.

members.appAdmins.tag.noAccount.description: Small tag beside "will be added" in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app: nobody has an account with the username typed. Lower case.

members.appAdmins.tag.noAccountTitle.text: No account with this username yet. They'll become an admin once they sign up and the app next deploys
members.appAdmins.tag.noAccountTitle.description: Tooltip of the "no account yet" tag in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app.

members.appAdmins.note.editable.text: Changes are proposed as a pull request editing <0>dapp.json</0>’s <1>admins</1> list. It needs real Yes votes and won’t merge on a timer.
members.appAdmins.note.editable.description: Note under the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app for someone who may edit the list. dapp.json is a file name and "admins" a setting in it: both stay as they are, inside their numbered tags. "Yes" is the name of the vote in favour.

members.appAdmins.note.readOnly.text: Set in <0>dapp.json</0>. To change them, open a pull request that edits the <1>admins</1> list. That proposal needs real Yes votes and won’t merge on a timer.
members.appAdmins.note.readOnly.description: Note under the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app for someone who may not edit the list. dapp.json is a file name and "admins" a setting in it: both stay as they are, inside their numbered tags. "Yes" is the name of the vote in favour.

members.appAdmins.alreadyWaiting.text: A change to the app's admins is already waiting for approval. See it in the Workshop.
members.appAdmins.alreadyWaiting.description: Status in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when an earlier proposal about the admins is undecided. The Workshop is a tab of the app's page; keep it as a name.

members.appAdmins.noRepository.text: Admin changes are proposed as a dapp.json pull request, and this app has no GitHub repository, so they're unavailable.
members.appAdmins.noRepository.description: Status in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when the list cannot be changed. dapp.json is a file name and stays as it is.

members.appAdmins.tooMany.text: An app can declare at most 20 admins.
members.appAdmins.tooMany.description: Error in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when a twenty-first admin is added.

members.appAdmins.confirm.title.description: Title of the confirmation asked before a change to an app's admins is put up as a proposal. "Open" is a verb.

members.appAdmins.confirm.message.text: Changing who administers this app opens a proposal. Because it grants app-level power, it will not merge on a timer: it needs real Yes votes to reach the app's normal threshold, and only a platform admin can force-merge it.
members.appAdmins.confirm.message.description: Body of the confirmation asked before a change to an app's admins is put up as a proposal. "Yes" is the name of the vote in favour; to force-merge is to apply a proposal without waiting for the vote.

members.appAdmins.confirm.messageEmptyin.text: This removes every app admin. Only the creator and platform admins will be able to manage the app. The change opens a proposal that needs real Yes votes and won't merge on a timer.
members.appAdmins.confirm.messageEmptyin.description: Body of that confirmation when the change removes all of the app's admins. "Yes" is the name of the vote in favour.

members.appAdmins.confirm.open.description: Confirming button of that confirmation: creates the proposal. "Open" is a verb.

members.appAdmins.opened.text: Proposal opened (PR #{{number}}). It needs the group's vote in the Dev tab before the new admins apply.
members.appAdmins.opened.description: Status in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app after the change was put up as a proposal. {{number}} is the number of its pull request (PR); keep the # before it. "Dev" is the name of a tab.

members.appAdmins.failed.text: Could not open the admins proposal: {{reason}}
members.appAdmins.failed.description: Error in the "App admins" section of the "Members & approvals" dialog of an app when the proposal could not be created. {{reason}} is the server's explanation or a short technical reason.

secrets.title.app.description: Heading of the secrets dialog for an ordinary app. The dialog lists the environment variables an app declares (its secrets: keys and passwords it needs) and lets admins set them; for Homeroom itself it is titled "Platform variables".

secrets.title.platform.description: Heading of the secrets dialog when it shows Homeroom's own environment variables.

secrets.subtitle.initial.text: Environment variables this app declares in<0>dapp.json</0>.
secrets.subtitle.initial.description: Line under the heading of the secrets dialog while its contents load. dapp.json is a file name and stays as it is, inside its numbered tag.

secrets.subtitle.app.text: Environment variables this app declares in <0>dapp.json</0>.
secrets.subtitle.app.description: Line under the heading of the secrets dialog for an ordinary app. dapp.json is a file name and stays as it is, inside its numbered tag.

secrets.subtitle.platform.text: The platform's own environment variables, declared in its <0>dapp.json</0>. <1>A change here is not live immediately: it is applied by the platform's next deploy.</1>
secrets.subtitle.platform.description: Line under the heading of the secrets dialog for Homeroom itself ("the platform"). dapp.json is a file name and stays as it is, inside tag 0; tag 1 makes the warning bold.

secrets.footer.text: Changes apply on the next deploy. Admins can<0>redeploy now</0>.
secrets.footer.description: Footer of the secrets dialog. The numbered tag is a link-like button that restarts the app with the new values at once.

secrets.redeploy.triggering.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog after "redeploy now" was pressed, while the request is sent.

secrets.redeploy.started.text: Redeploy started. Watch the version pill.
secrets.redeploy.started.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog once the redeploy began. The version pill is the small label on the app's page that shows which version is running.

secrets.redeploy.failed.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when the redeploy could not be started. {{reason}} is the server's explanation or a short technical reason.

secrets.loadFailed.description: Error in place of the list in the secrets dialog. {{reason}} is a short technical reason such as "HTTP 500".

secrets.noManifest.text: No manifest snapshot yet. Once this app's first deploy completes the declared secrets show up here.
secrets.noManifest.description: Note at the top of the list in the secrets dialog for an app that has never been deployed. The manifest is the app's dapp.json file.

secrets.empty.platform.text: No platform variables are declared yet. Use “New variable” below to declare the first one.
secrets.empty.platform.description: Shown in place of the list in the secrets dialog for Homeroom itself. “New variable” is the button under the list; translate it as that button.

secrets.empty.app.text: This app's <0>dapp.json</0> doesn't declare any secrets yet. Use “New secret” below to declare the first one.
secrets.empty.app.description: Shown in place of the list in the secrets dialog for an app. dapp.json is a file name and stays as it is, inside its numbered tag. “New secret” is the button under the list.

secrets.state.set.description: Badge on a variable's row in the secrets dialog: the variable has a value. An adjective, not a command.

secrets.state.unset.description: Badge on a variable's row in the secrets dialog: the variable has no value, so any default applies.

secrets.state.managed.description: Badge on a variable's row in the secrets dialog: the value is written by the deploy process and cannot be set here.

secrets.state.orphan.description: Badge on a variable's row in the secrets dialog: a value is still stored but dapp.json no longer lists the variable.

secrets.state.proposed.description: Badge on a variable's row in the secrets dialog: adding this variable is a proposal that has not been voted in yet.

secrets.badge.required.description: Small upper-cased tag on a variable's row in the secrets dialog: the app cannot deploy without a value for it.

secrets.badge.sensitive.description: Small upper-cased tag on a variable's row in the secrets dialog: the value is secret and is hidden once saved.

secrets.badge.sensitiveTitle.description: Tooltip of the "sensitive" tag on a variable's row in the secrets dialog.

secrets.badge.orphan.description: Small upper-cased tag on a variable's row in the secrets dialog: a value is stored for a variable the app no longer declares.

secrets.github.note.text: Read-only. Change these in the repo's <0>Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions</0> on GitHub. GitHub never returns a secret's value to anyone, so only the name and when it last changed can be shown here.
secrets.github.note.description: Note under the "GitHub Actions secrets" heading in the secrets dialog. The numbered tag holds the path to a page of GitHub's settings; use the names GitHub shows.

secrets.github.noteStaged.text: Read-only. Change these in the repo's <0>Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions</0> on GitHub. GitHub never returns a secret's value to anyone, so only the name and when it last changed can be shown here. <1>(Staging preview: this list is demo data.)</1>
secrets.github.noteStaged.description: The same note on a staging preview, where the list is made up. Tag 0 holds the path to a page of GitHub's settings; tag 1 sets the last remark in italics.

secrets.github.noteNone.text: No Actions secrets on this repo. Read-only. Change these in the repo's <0>Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions</0> on GitHub. GitHub never returns a secret's value to anyone, so only the name and when it last changed can be shown here.
secrets.github.noteNone.description: Note under the "GitHub Actions secrets" heading in the secrets dialog when the repository has none. The numbered tag holds the path to a page of GitHub's settings; use the names GitHub shows.

secrets.github.unavailable.text: Couldn't read the platform repo's Actions secrets.
secrets.github.unavailable.description: Amber note under the "GitHub Actions secrets" heading in the secrets dialog when GitHub could not be asked and gave no reason. "Platform repo" is Homeroom's own code repository.

secrets.value.github.description: In place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog for a GitHub Actions secret: it exists on GitHub and its value cannot be read.

secrets.value.githubUpdated.description: In place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog for a GitHub Actions secret. {{date}} is when it last changed, already formatted, such as Oct 8, 2026. Keep the middle dot as a separator.

secrets.value.proposed.text: value included, applied when the proposal merges
secrets.value.proposed.description: In place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog whose declaration is waiting for approval: a value was sent with the proposal. Lower case.

secrets.value.proposedEnding.text: value included (…{{ending}}), applied when the proposal merges
secrets.value.proposedEnding.description: The same, showing the end of the proposed value. {{ending}} is its last four characters; keep the ellipsis before it.

secrets.value.declarationOnly.description: In place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog whose declaration is waiting for approval and came without a value. Lower case.

secrets.value.private.description: In place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog marked private. Keep the dots, which stand for the hidden value.

secrets.value.unreadable.text: set, but the stored value could not be read
secrets.value.unreadable.description: In place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog when a value is stored but could not be decrypted. Lower case.

secrets.value.setEnding.description: In place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog that has one. {{ending}} is the value's last four characters; keep the ellipsis before it. "set" is an adjective, lower case.

secrets.value.setHidden.description: In place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog that has one of which nothing may be shown. Keep the dots. "set" is an adjective, lower case.

secrets.value.missing.description: In red, in place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog that is required and has none. Lower case.

secrets.value.default.description: In place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog with no value of its own. {{fallback}} is the default value written in dapp.json, shown as it is.

secrets.value.notSet.description: In place of a value on a variable's row in the secrets dialog with neither a value nor a default. Lower case.

secrets.action.set.description: Small lower-case button on a variable's row in the secrets dialog for an admin: asks for a value and stores it at once. A verb.

secrets.action.replace.description: Small lower-case button on a variable's row in the secrets dialog that already has a value, for an admin: asks for a new value and stores it at once. A verb.

secrets.action.clear.description: Small lower-case button on a variable's row in the secrets dialog for an admin: deletes the stored value. A verb.

secrets.action.proposeSet.description: Small lower-case button on a variable's row in the secrets dialog: puts setting a value up for the group's vote instead of storing it at once.

secrets.action.proposeReplace.description: Small lower-case button on a variable's row in the secrets dialog that already has a value: puts replacing it up for the group's vote.

secrets.action.proposeClear.description: Small lower-case button on a variable's row in the secrets dialog: puts deleting the stored value up for the group's vote.

secrets.action.viewProposal.description: Link on a variable's row in the secrets dialog whose declaration is waiting for approval: opens the app's page where that proposal is.

secrets.action.viewProposalNumbered.description: The same link when the proposal's pull request number is known. {{number}} is that number; keep the # before it.

secrets.row.githubStored.text: Stored as an Actions secret on the platform repo. Its value can't be shown, because GitHub's API never returns one. Change it in the repo's Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions.
secrets.row.githubStored.description: Note on a GitHub Actions secret's row in the secrets dialog. The last three names are the path to a page of GitHub's settings; use the names GitHub shows.

secrets.row.deployManaged.text: Set by the deploy from a GitHub secret. It can't be edited here.
secrets.row.deployManaged.description: Note on a variable's row in the secrets dialog whose value the deploy process writes.

secrets.row.alsoGithub.text: Also a GitHub Actions secret on the platform repo.
secrets.row.alsoGithub.description: Note on a variable's row in the secrets dialog that also exists as a secret on GitHub.

secrets.row.alsoGithubUpdated.text: Also a GitHub Actions secret on the platform repo · updated {{date}}.
secrets.row.alsoGithubUpdated.description: Note on a variable's row in the secrets dialog that also exists as a secret on GitHub. {{date}} is when that one last changed, already formatted. Keep the middle dot as a separator.

secrets.row.proposed.text: Not declared yet. A change adding it to <0>dapp.json</0> is waiting for approval.
secrets.row.proposed.description: Note on a variable's row in the secrets dialog that is only proposed. dapp.json is a file name and stays as it is, inside its numbered tag.

secrets.row.proposedBy.text: Not declared yet. A change adding it to <0>dapp.json</0> is waiting for approval (opened by {{person}}).
secrets.row.proposedBy.description: The same note naming who proposed it. {{person}} is their username. dapp.json stays as it is, inside its numbered tag.

secrets.row.pendingDeclaration.text: Value set · its declaration is waiting for approval.
secrets.row.pendingDeclaration.description: Note on a variable's row in the secrets dialog whose value is stored while the proposal that declares it is undecided. Keep the middle dot as a separator.

secrets.row.pendingDeclarationNumbered.text: Value set · its declaration is waiting for approval (PR #{{number}}).
secrets.row.pendingDeclarationNumbered.description: The same note with the proposal's pull request (PR) number. {{number}} is that number; keep the # before it.

secrets.row.orphan.text: No longer declared in <0>dapp.json</0>. Its value is kept so a rollback still works, so clear it once you're sure.
secrets.row.orphan.description: Note on a variable's row in the secrets dialog the app no longer declares. dapp.json stays as it is, inside its numbered tag. A rollback is returning to an earlier version of the app.

secrets.declare.open.variable.description: Button under the list in the secrets dialog for Homeroom itself: opens the form that declares a new variable. Keep the plus sign.

secrets.declare.open.secret.description: Button under the list in the secrets dialog for an app: opens the form that declares a new secret. Keep the plus sign.

secrets.declare.unavailable.description: Beside the "+ New variable" button in the secrets dialog when declaring is switched off and the server gave no reason.

secrets.declare.hint.direct.text: Declares it in dapp.json (a proposal) and stores your value now.
secrets.declare.hint.direct.description: Beside the "+ New variable" button in the secrets dialog, for an admin. dapp.json is a file name and stays as it is.

secrets.declare.hint.proposal.text: Declaration and value wait for approval together.
secrets.declare.hint.proposal.description: Beside the "+ New variable" button in the secrets dialog, for someone who is not an admin.

secrets.declare.heading.platform.description: Heading of the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog for Homeroom itself.

secrets.declare.heading.app.description: Heading of the form in the secrets dialog that declares a new secret, for an ordinary app.

secrets.declare.blocked.text: New variables can't be declared right now.
secrets.declare.blocked.description: Amber note at the top of the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog when declaring is switched off and the server gave no reason.

secrets.declare.blockedStatus.text: New variables can't be declared right now.
secrets.declare.blockedStatus.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when the form was submitted while declaring is switched off and the server gave no reason.

secrets.declare.key.label.description: Label of the field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog for the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY. "Key" as in key and value, not a key that opens something.

secrets.declare.key.help.text: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE: the name your code reads from the environment.
secrets.declare.key.help.description: Help under the Key field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog. UPPER_SNAKE_CASE shows the required spelling (capitals joined by underscores) and stays as it is.

secrets.declare.description.label.description: Label of the field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog for a short explanation of the variable.

secrets.declare.description.placeholder.text: What this value is and where to get it
secrets.declare.description.placeholder.description: Greyed text inside the empty Description field of the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog.

secrets.declare.value.label.description: Label of the field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog for the variable's value.

secrets.declare.value.placeholder.description: Greyed text inside the empty Value field of the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog: with no value, only the declaration is made.

secrets.declare.value.helpDirect.text: Stored as soon as you submit. Optional if you give a default below.
secrets.declare.value.helpDirect.description: Help under the Value field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog, for an admin.

secrets.declare.value.helpProposal.text: Held encrypted and stored when the proposal merges. Optional if you give a default below.
secrets.declare.value.helpProposal.description: Help under the Value field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog, for someone who is not an admin.

secrets.declare.required.description: Checkbox in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog: the app cannot deploy until this variable has a value.

secrets.declare.private.description: Checkbox in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog: the value is encrypted and never shown again.

secrets.declare.flagsHelp.platform.text: Required blocks deploys until it has a value. Private means encrypted at rest and never displayed again.
secrets.declare.flagsHelp.platform.description: Help under the Required and Private checkboxes in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog, for Homeroom itself. Translate "Required" and "Private" as the checkboxes are.

secrets.declare.flagsHelp.app.text: Required blocks deploys until it has a value. Private means encrypted at rest and never displayed again, and never copied into PR previews.
secrets.declare.flagsHelp.app.description: Help under the Required and Private checkboxes in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog, for an app. A PR preview is a test copy of the app built for a proposal.

secrets.declare.default.label.description: Label of the field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog for the value used when none is set. A noun.

secrets.declare.default.placeholder.description: Greyed text inside the empty Default field of the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog.

secrets.declare.default.helpPlatform.text: Documents the fallback your code already uses. The platform's deploy does not apply it, so set a value above if the variable really needs one.
secrets.declare.default.helpPlatform.description: Help under the Default field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog, for Homeroom itself.

secrets.declare.default.helpApp.text: Used at deploy time when no value is stored.
secrets.declare.default.helpApp.description: Help under the Default field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog, for an app.

secrets.declare.group.label.description: Label of the field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog for the heading the variable is listed under.

secrets.declare.group.help.text: The heading this row files under in this panel.
secrets.declare.group.help.description: Help under the Group field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog. "This panel" is the secrets dialog.

secrets.declare.stagingDefault.label.description: Label of the field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog for the value test copies (PR previews) of the app use.

secrets.declare.stagingDefault.placehold.description: Greyed text inside the empty Staging default field of the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog.

secrets.declare.stagingDefault.help.text: What PR previews use. A required + private secret needs one (or a default), otherwise no preview of this app can boot.
secrets.declare.stagingDefault.help.description: Help under the Staging default field in the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog. A PR preview is a test copy of the app built for a proposal.

secrets.declare.submit.direct.description: Submit button of the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog, for an admin: declares the variable and stores its value.

secrets.declare.submit.variable.description: Submit button of the "New variable" form of the secrets dialog for Homeroom itself, for someone who is not an admin: puts the declaration up for a vote.

secrets.declare.submit.secret.description: Submit button of the same form for an app, for someone who is not an admin: puts the declaration up for a vote.

secrets.declare.error.key.text: Key must be UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (letters, digits and underscores).
secrets.declare.error.key.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when the typed name is not capitals, digits and underscores. UPPER_SNAKE_CASE stays as it is.

secrets.declare.error.requiredValue.text: A required variable needs either a value or a default.
secrets.declare.error.requiredValue.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when Required is ticked and both Value and Default are empty.

secrets.declare.error.stagingDefault.text: PR previews of this app won't boot without a staging default for a required private secret.
secrets.declare.error.stagingDefault.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when a required private secret has neither a staging default nor a default.

secrets.declare.error.quote.text: Values can't contain a single quote or a carriage return. They wouldn't survive being written to the platform's .env file.
secrets.declare.error.quote.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when a value for Homeroom itself contains a character that cannot be stored. .env is a file name.

secrets.declare.opening.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog while the proposal declaring a new variable is created. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.declare.opened.stored.text: Proposal opened for {{key}}. Your value is stored; the declaration still needs a merge vote.
secrets.declare.opened.stored.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog after an admin declared a new variable. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.declare.opened.storedNumbered.text: Proposal opened for {{key}} (PR #{{number}}). Your value is stored; the declaration still needs a merge vote.
secrets.declare.opened.storedNumbered.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog after an admin declared a new variable. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY. {{number}} is the pull request's number; keep the # before it.

secrets.declare.opened.pending.text: Proposal opened for {{key}}. Vote on it in the group chat panel. The value applies when it merges.
secrets.declare.opened.pending.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog after a new variable was proposed. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.declare.opened.pendingNumbered.text: Proposal opened for {{key}} (PR #{{number}}). Vote on it in the group chat panel. The value applies when it merges.
secrets.declare.opened.pendingNumbered.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog after a new variable was proposed. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY. {{number}} is the pull request's number; keep the # before it.

secrets.declare.failed.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when the proposal declaring a new variable could not be created. {{reason}} is the server's explanation or a short technical reason.

secrets.set.title.description: Title of the small dialog that asks an admin for a variable's value. "Set" is a verb. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.set.sensitive.text: This value is sensitive: it is encrypted at rest and never shown again.
secrets.set.sensitive.description: Message in the small dialog that asks an admin for the value of a variable marked sensitive.

secrets.set.placeholder.description: Greyed text inside the empty field of the small dialog that asks an admin for a variable's value.

secrets.set.setting.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog while a value is being stored. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.set.saved.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog after a value was stored. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.set.failed.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when a value could not be stored. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY. {{reason}} is the server's explanation or a short technical reason.

secrets.clear.title.description: Title of the confirmation asked before an admin deletes a variable's stored value. "Clear" is a verb. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.clear.confirm.description: Confirming button of that confirmation: deletes the stored value. A verb.

secrets.clear.clearing.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog while a stored value is being deleted. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.clear.cleared.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog after a stored value was deleted. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.clear.failed.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when a stored value could not be deleted. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY. {{reason}} is the server's explanation or a short technical reason.

secrets.proposeSet.title.description: Title of the small dialog that asks for a value to put up for the group's vote. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.proposeSet.message.text: A majority of active users must vote up before this applies.
secrets.proposeSet.message.description: Message in the small dialog that asks for a value to put up for the group's vote. To vote up is to vote in favour.

secrets.proposeSet.messageSensitive.text: This value is sensitive. A majority of active users must vote up before this applies.
secrets.proposeSet.messageSensitive.description: The same message for a variable marked sensitive.

secrets.proposeSet.placeholder.description: Greyed text inside the empty field of the small dialog that asks for a value to put up for the group's vote.

secrets.proposeSet.confirm.description: Confirming button of that small dialog: creates the proposal. A verb.

secrets.proposeSet.opening.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog while the proposal to set a value is created. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.proposeSet.opened.text: Proposal opened. Vote in the group chat tab.
secrets.proposeSet.opened.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog after the proposal to set a value was created.

secrets.proposeSet.failed.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when the proposal to set a value could not be created. {{reason}} is the server's explanation or a short technical reason.

secrets.proposeClear.title.description: Title of the confirmation asked before deleting a variable's value is put up for the group's vote. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.proposeClear.confirm.description: Confirming button of that confirmation: creates the proposal. A verb.

secrets.proposeClear.opening.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog while the proposal to delete a value is created. {{key}} is the variable's name, such as STRIPE_API_KEY.

secrets.proposeClear.opened.text: Proposal opened. Vote in the group chat tab.
secrets.proposeClear.opened.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog after the proposal to delete a value was created.

secrets.proposeClear.failed.description: Status line at the bottom of the secrets dialog, in red, when the proposal to delete a value could not be created. {{reason}} is the server's explanation or a short technical reason.

screenshot.hint.text: Drag to select the area to capture. Esc to cancel
screenshot.hint.description: Instruction at the top of the screenshot overlay of the "Suggest an improvement" dialog, where the person drags a rectangle over a frozen picture of the page to choose what to attach. Esc is the Escape key and stays as it is.

screenshot.attach.description: Accessible name of the check-mark button in the screenshot overlay of the "Suggest an improvement" dialog, where the person drags a rectangle over a frozen picture of the page to choose what to attach: attaches the marked area as a picture.

screenshot.cancel.description: Accessible name of the X button in the screenshot overlay of the "Suggest an improvement" dialog, where the person drags a rectangle over a frozen picture of the page to choose what to attach: leaves without attaching anything.
